title: Reflux vs GERD — what's normal spitting up?
summary: Most reflux is normal baby spit-up. GERD is when reflux causes pain or poor growth.
whatsNormal:
Gastroesophageal reflux (GER) is milk coming back up from a still-maturing valve between stomach and esophagus.

• Small spit-up after most feeds is common in the first months
• Happy baby between episodes
• Steady weight gain at checkups
• Often improves by 4–6 months as baby sits more and eats solids

Keeping baby upright 20–30 minutes after feeds and smaller, more frequent feeds can help mild reflux. Thickening or medication is only for cases your clinician identifies.
watchFor: Arching back, crying, or refusing feeds consistently
Poor weight gain or dropping percentiles on growth charts
Chronic cough, wheeze, or hoarse cry
callDoctorIf: Green (bile) or bloody spit-up or vomit
Signs of dehydration or fever under 3 months
Baby in clear pain during or after every feed
You wonder if this is more than normal spit-up — a visit can clarify
